title: Bidirectional A* in San Francisco: Routing ⚡
description: See how Bidirectional A* shrinks search time by expanding from both start and goal until the frontiers meet. In this real-map visualization, milliseconds matter—just like autonomous vehicle routing.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — how autonomous vehicles & routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

Picture the city grid as a graph: roads are edges, intersections are nodes. Bidirectional A* runs two A* searches at once—one forward from your start, one backward from your destination—each guided by a heuristic (think: “distance-to-go” estimates).

Why it’s fast:
✅ It reduces the search space vs single-direction A*
✅ It stops early when the two waves meet
✅ It still uses optimality guarantees when heuristics behave well

Takeaway: when speed matters, meeting-in-the-middle can beat expanding everywhere.

Debate question: would you rather maximize optimality safety (more exploration) or minimize latency (aggressive early meeting)?
